title: Stale KS_eigenvector_* / Cs_data_* leftovers are symlinks, so the cleanup script silently skips them
symptom: After cleanup, 'residual' KS_eigenvector_* and Cs_data_* entries remain in GW directories (e.g. gw_inputs_k888_shrink and C_supercell_gw_512_1024_20260518/C1024), so old outputs keep appearing to belong to the current run.
root_cause: Those leftovers are symbolic links, not regular files: the previous cleanup script skips symlinks by default as a safety measure, so they were never removed. Old outputs therefore remain visible in a directory that is supposed to have been cleaned.
minimal_fix: Inspect the link targets first (ls -l / readlink -f), then remove the links themselves (unlink or rm on the link, never recursing into the target), and update the cleanup procedure to handle symlinks explicitly instead of skipping them silently.
validation: Re-list the cleaned directories with `find <dir> -type l` plus ls -l and confirm no stale KS_eigenvector_*/Cs_data_* links remain while their targets still exist; disk usage should drop by the intended amount.
avoid: Do not delete with a recursive follow-symlink operation (it risks wiping the real data the links point at), and do not conclude the cleanup failed for permission reasons before checking whether the leftovers are symlinks.

parameters.cleanup_symlink_rule: detect symlinks (test -L / find -type l) and unlink them explicitly; never follow them recursively
